procedure.description: insertion of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator with transvenous lead

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Silverline Medicare Advantage denied the claim for CPT 33249 (insertion of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator with transvenous lead) with date of service 2026-06-09. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish an ejection fraction of 35 percent or less after an adequate trial of guideline-directed medical therapy.

criteria.text: Left ventricular ejection fraction of 35 percent or less on echocardiography, nuclear study, or cardiac MRI, measured after at least 90 days of guideline-directed medical therapy.
New York Heart Association class II or III heart failure symptoms.

At least 90 days of guideline-directed medical therapy including a beta blocker and an ACE inhibitor, ARB, or ARNI, with a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist and an SGLT2 inhibitor as tolerated, at maximally tolerated doses.
More than 40 days after any myocardial infarction and more than 90 days after any coronary revascularization.
Expected survival with good functional status of more than one year.

chart.text: Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for evaluation. His history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.

63 year old man in cardiology clinic for ischemic cardiomyopathy after his infarction. Reviewed the plan: optimize medications, repeat the echo in 3 months, and decide on a defibrillator then. He understands the device is for sudden death prevention, not symptoms. His history otherwise: anxiety, sees a counselor, seasonal allergies. Allergies: sulfa, hives as a child. Quit smoking 15 years ago, no alcohol, retired. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Anterior ST-elevation infarction 11 months ago, drug-eluting stent to the proximal left anterior descending at that time. No revascularization since; no residual ischemia on the follow-up stress study. No other life-limiting illness, independent, still working. Expected survival well over a year.
Transthoracic echocardiogram. Left ventricular ejection fraction 24 percent by biplane Simpson’s, anterior and apical akinesis, mild mitral regurgitation, no thrombus.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

Carvedilol 25 twice daily, sacubitril-valsartan 97/103 twice daily, spironolactone 25 daily, empagliflozin 10 daily. All four started after the infarction and titrated to these doses by the second cardiology visit; doses unchanged since.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, he will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

Here with a cough and congestion for 4 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if he gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the scheduler.
Blood pressure check. 128 over 72 today, 139 over 84 on repeat. He has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 8 weeks.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 2.1, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 100. Repeat in a year.
Check-in while we wait on the insurance. No change in the complaints. Reviewed the risks and recovery one more time, he remains sure about going ahead.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 6 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. He mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

Three-month visit. Reviewed the repeat echocardiogram with him. Discussed primary prevention defibrillator, risks of implant, what a shock feels like, driving rules. Decision made today. Vitals today 119 over 90, pulse 71. Short of breath carrying groceries up one flight, fine on the flat, no orthopnea now. Class II to III. 92 days on full guideline-directed therapy at target doses, tolerating, potassium 4.7, blood pressure 110 over 67.

Repeat transthoracic echocardiogram after 3 months of optimized medical therapy. Left ventricular ejection fraction improved to 42 percent by biplane Simpson’s. Anterior wall hypokinetic rather than akinetic.

Called his with the cholesterol results. Total 208, LDL 108, HDL 57, triglycerides 125. Discussed diet and walking. He wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.
Pre-procedure visit for device implant. Hold the apixaban one dose, continue the rest. Chest X-ray and labs fine. Consent signed.

expected.note: The chart raises crit-1 (ef) but does not satisfy it; the mention is a plan, a shortfall, or a result below the threshold.
